title: Family and friends protest Keyla Martínez's death in police custody
location: Outside the police post, La Esperanza, Intibucá
threshold_50_evidence: Peoples Dispatch explicitly reports hundreds outside the La Esperanza station after news of Keyla Martínez’s death. This is a qualitative estimate above 50 for the initial gathering; it is not applied to later dates or other cities. Its Criterio photo credit does not establish shared reporting.

occurrence.summary: Proceso describes a nighttime protest outside La Esperanza police post on 7 February by family and friends demanding clarification and justice for Keyla Martínez’s death in custody. Peoples Dispatch reports hundreds protesting outside the same station after news of her death; the location, date and grievance align with this initial gathering.

start_date.summary: Proceso dates publication to 7 February and states the protest occurred that Sunday night. Peoples Dispatch dates Keyla’s death to early 7 February.

location.summary: Outside the police post in La Esperanza, Intibucá, western Honduras.

demands.summary: The participants demanded clarification of the death; the article also says family members demanded justice.

participants.summary: Peoples Dispatch says hundreds protested outside the station after news of the death; no exact count is supplied.

state_response.summary: No response is assigned to this 7 February gathering. Peoples Dispatch reports force against protests continuing over following days without allocating it to this date. The prior custody death is the grievance, not protest-period violence.

organizer.summary: Family and friends are identified as participants, but no organizer is named.

notes: The initial gathering is supported by two contemporary reports at the same station: Proceso places family/friends there Sunday night, and Peoples Dispatch reports hundreds there after the news broke. Later actions in the continuing justice wave remain separate candidates with unresolved exact continuity.
open_questions: Confirm whether later La Esperanza actions were separate gatherings or a continuous assembly; keep city/date detail if separate.
Resolve the amount and event-level distribution of injuries and state responses across later actions.

title: Justice protest outside La Esperanza police post met with tear gas and rubber bullets
location: Outside the police post, La Esperanza, Intibucá
threshold_50_evidence: The report describes the gathering but supplies no assembled-person estimate; an attendance threshold of 50 is not established.

occurrence.summary: Conexihon reports a first protest one day after Keyla Martínez's death outside the police post where she died; it says police used tear gas and rubber bullets.

start_date.summary: Conexihon places the first repression one day after Keyla’s death; Peoples Dispatch dates her death to early 7 February, yielding 8 February for this report-described action.

location.summary: Outside the police post, La Esperanza, Intibucá

demands.summary: The action demanded justice for Keyla Martínez after her death in police custody.

participants.summary: The report provides no assembled-person estimate; detentions/injuries are not a turnout count.

state_response.summary: Conexihon reports tear gas and rubber bullets during the first La Esperanza repression. Peoples Dispatch describes heavy police/Special Forces repression in the continuing days but does not allocate every method or injury to this gathering.

organizer.summary: The report describes self-convened citizens; it names no formal organizer.

notes: Conexihon describes a first repression one day after the 7 February death; Peoples Dispatch anchors the date as 8 February. Kept separate from the initial 7 February nighttime gathering and the later sit-in.
open_questions: Establish simultaneous attendance of at least 50.
Confirm whether this is a distinct assembly from E001 and what exact force/injuries occurred at this date.

title: Second justice sit-in in La Esperanza repressed by police
threshold_50_evidence: The report describes the gathering but supplies no assembled-person estimate; an attendance threshold of 50 is not established.

occurrence.summary: Conexihon describes another peaceful sit-in two days after Keyla Martínez's death and reports that police again repressed it.

start_date.summary: Conexihon places the second sit-in two days after Keyla’s death; Peoples Dispatch dates her death to early 7 February, yielding 9 February for this report-described action.

demands.summary: The action demanded justice for Keyla Martínez after her death in police custody.

participants.summary: The report provides no assembled-person estimate; detentions/injuries are not a turnout count.

state_response.summary: Conexihon says police again repressed the peaceful sit-in; Peoples Dispatch reports repression continuing over following days. Tear gas, rubber bullets, batons and at least four injuries are not all attributed to this specific gathering.

organizer.summary: The report describes self-convened citizens; it names no formal organizer.

notes: Conexihon describes a second peaceful sit-in two days after the 7 February death; Peoples Dispatch anchors the date as 9 February. Kept separate from the initial protest and the day-after repression.
open_questions: Establish simultaneous attendance of at least 50.
Determine specific response methods and injury attribution for this sit-in.

title: Choluteca justice mobilization following Keyla Martínez’s death
threshold_50_evidence: The report describes the gathering but supplies no assembled-person estimate; an attendance threshold of 50 is not established.

occurrence.summary: Conexihon reports that citizens mobilized in Choluteca demanding justice for Keyla Martínez and denounced police surveillance of participants.

start_date.summary: Both reports describe a Choluteca action after Keyla’s death, but neither assigns an exact calendar date to that city gathering.

demands.summary: The action demanded justice for Keyla Martínez after her death in police custody.

participants.summary: The report provides no assembled-person estimate; detentions/injuries are not a turnout count.

state_response.summary: A surveillance complaint is not one of the coded seven response fields; the article does not establish a protest-specific arrest, beating, dispersal, accommodation, or other coded response in Choluteca.

organizer.summary: The report describes self-convened citizens; it names no formal organizer.

notes: A local justice mobilization in Choluteca is reported separately from the La Esperanza gatherings and the dated Tegucigalpa protest; no date, crowd size or specific response is established.
open_questions: Establish exact event date and simultaneous attendance of at least 50.
Verify the surveillance allegation and any separately attributable state response.

title: Tegucigalpa justice demonstration with five student arrests
threshold_50_evidence: The report describes the gathering but supplies no assembled-person estimate; an attendance threshold of 50 is not established.

occurrence.summary: Conexihon describes a demonstration joined by students, human-rights representatives and residents; it reports five student detentions during the action and their later release by a judge after a hearing.

start_date.summary: Peoples Dispatch dates the Tegucigalpa protest to 10 February 2021.

demands.summary: The action demanded justice for Keyla Martínez after her death in police custody.

participants.summary: Students, human-rights representatives and residents are identified; the five detained students are not a turnout estimate.

state_response.summary: Both reports describe five student detentions during the protest. Conexihon reports their later release by a judge after a hearing; this is not coded as accommodation of the protest demand.

notes: Peoples Dispatch gives the event date as 10 February; both Peoples Dispatch and Conexihon report five student arrests. The arrest count does not establish overall attendance.
open_questions: Establish simultaneous attendance of at least 50.
Verify the detentions and exact charging/release chronology.
